title: Leveraging Big Data to Study Information Dissemination of Material Firm Events

scopes.description: The one supplied SAS program's complete author-documented workflow through its generated main samples; no analysis-only scope is supported because no compatible prepared sample or Stata analysis driver is supplied.

requirements.description: The supplied program imports the author-named Orbital refinery workbook and derives the refinery/event panel used by every later stage. The release contains only code and the datasheet, so compatible file presence, columns and coverage are not established.

software.name: SAS 9.4, SAS/CONNECT/WRDS, SAS/ETS, and DBMS format support
software.description: The supplied program uses SAS and SAS/CONNECT RSUBMIT to WRDS. It also invokes local PROC EXPAND after ENDRSUBMIT and imports/exports using DBMS=XLSX and DBMS=STATA. The environment record reports SAS could not initialize TKELS, which does not establish an absent license or working local/remote execution. Selected-host SAS/ETS availability and XLSX/STATA DBMS or format support remain unverified; no component absence is established. The official 2024.09 guide identifies the SAS/ETS family but does not certify SAS 9.4 host compatibility.

software.name: Spreadsheet application for the manual refinery crosswalk

issues.description: The datasheet documents Orbital data obtained under an NDA and says sample identifiers are withheld; it does not establish a present compatible dataset route or authorize assuming the agreement bars all permitted replication use. The matching workbook is a separate manual handoff.
RR2_IBES and OIL_INDEX have no supplied producers, and the code writes GASBUDDY but later reads GASBUDDY_CLEAN. These are distinct closure gaps pending author source/contract clarification.

SAS launch, WRDS credentials/connection, remote libraries and a Dropbox macro/path setup are not verified for this environment. In addition, local SAS/ETS availability for PROC EXPAND after ENDRSUBMIT and selected-host support for the authored DBMS=XLSX import and DBMS=STATA export remain unverified; neither is a finding of absence. The SAS/ETS guide-family title does not establish SAS 9.4 host compatibility. Existing SAS initialization failure is not evidence of missing entitlement; path/root/log configuration remains ordinary preparation.
Step 10 uses &interval before the only in-file assignment at Step 11, which selects month and comments out quarter. The intended Step 10 interval cannot be inferred from the later definition.

Six bounded one-row probes establish readability and columns for selected Compustat/CRSP/FF tables only. They do not verify the required firm population, quarterly lags, daily event windows, monthly source bounds, or forward-return tails; CRSP.MSEDELIST and author-prepared inputs remain unprobed.

dependency_review.description: The first XLSX read is the exact author-named Orbital input; its compatible route remains unverified.
Step 1 imports the manually reviewed refinery_orbital_v1.xlsx crosswalk after exporting rows for matching.
The combined author workbook supplies Bloomberg and Factiva event fields used to derive orbital_new.
The remote SAS block reads COMP.FUNDQ; a local one-row probe confirms selected columns but not the required history.
The daily CRSP block joins CRSP.DSEDELIST by PERMNO and date.
The daily CRSP branch joins FF.FACTORS_DAILY by date.
The event-return stage reads the unproduced RR2_IBES table and requires OFTIC, PENDS and ANNDATS; catalog candidates do not close the mapping.

These are authored intermediates/outputs produced in source order: orbital_new feeds rr2_fundq; CRSP/FF stages produce rr2_dsf and rr2_msf, then rr2_dsf1 and rr2_msf1; Step 5 produces oil_acq_cost and firm_capacity; Steps 7-11 produce rr2_orbital, the gas-price, ROA and media samples, and the monthly return sample. actions.description: After input, software and contract gaps are resolved, follow the eleven supplied SAS stages in source order; the trace records the producer/consumer chains and all checklist IDs.
steps: Import Orbital, manually match and return refinery_orbital_v1.xlsx, merge the combined Bloomberg/Factiva workbook, and write REFINERY.orbital_new.
Join REFINERY.orbital_new firm keys to COMP.FUNDQ, construct the authored one-quarter/four-quarter lags, and write REFINERY.rr2_fundq.

Read CRSP.DSF, CRSP.DSEDELIST and FF.FACTORS_DAILY over the Orbital-derived bounds and write REFINERY.rr2_dsf. Join rr2_fundq, the unresolved RR2_IBES handoff and rr2_dsf, apply the author event-window procedure and oil_index joins, and write rr2_dsf1.
